headlines.title_en: Two-year German bond yield rises over 4 basis points; Warsh signals hawkish stance in Jackson Hole debut
headlines.summary_en: In late European trading on Friday (August 28), the yield on Germany's 10-year Bund rose 2.6 basis points to 3.279%. After Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish tone in his Jackson Hole speech released at 22:00 Beijing time, yields briefly turned lower, then fell again around 22:44, ending the week up 2.0 basis points with a V-shaped reversal overall. The 2-year Bund yield rose 4.2 basis points to 2.906%, expanding gains notably after Warsh's speech, up 5.8 basis points on the week, having dipped to 2.784% before European markets opened on August 26 before trending higher; the 30-year Bund yield rose 1.3 basis points to 3.768%. The 2/10-year Bund yield spread fell 1.697 basis points to +36.990 basis points, up 0.006 basis point on the week.

headlines.title_en: Spot gold fell about 3.1%, as Wosh's remarks leaned hawkish
headlines.summary_en: At the New York close on Friday (August 28), spot gold fell 3.08% to $4,457.57 per ounce. When Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech text was released at 22:00 Beijing time, gold edged up to a session high of $4,631.61, then broke out of the prolonged narrow intraday range and fell rapidly. Gold declined 3.22% for the week, having traded in a tight range from Monday until Warsh's speech, forming a period top. Spot silver fell 4.17% to $66.3390 per ounce, down 3.89% for the week. COMEX copper futures fell 0.84% to $6.6330 per pound, down 0.73% for the week.

headlines.title_en: The U.S. dollar index rose over 0.5% this week, as Wosh struck a hawkish tone at the Jackson Hole central bank symposium
headlines.summary_en: At the New York close on Friday (August 28), the ICE U.S. Dollar Index rose 0.54% to 99.698 points. When Fed Chair Warsh's speech text was released at 22:00 Beijing time, it dipped to a session low of 99.098 points, then quickly rebounded to near 99.600 points. The index rose 0.90% for the week, having maintained a steady uptrend before Warsh's hawkish signals accelerated gains. The Bloomberg Dollar Index rose 0.39% to 1,198.98 points, up 0.62% for the week, trading in a range of 1,190.85-1,199.43 points.

headlines.title: 贝森特表示日元的无序波动将导致美国利率上升
headlines.summary: 美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特8月27日致信民主党参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦，为其上月动用外汇稳定基金（ESF）干预日元汇率进行辩护。贝森特表示，日元市场出现无序波动可能引发日本作为美债主要持有国的被迫平仓，从而破坏全球市场稳定，最终推高美国家庭和企业的借贷成本。他拒绝透露干预投入资金规模，仅确认使用ESF现有外币资产购买日元，并曾暗示动用欧元。日本上月为支撑日元投入创纪录的964亿美元。贝森特强调行动合法合规，美方未向日方提供任何信贷。信中他多次挖苦沃伦，建议她“上国际金融入门课程”。两人在国会听证会上素有紧张交锋。

headlines.title_en: Bessent said that disorderly yen fluctuations would lead to higher U.S. interest rates
headlines.summary_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wrote to Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren on August 27, defending his use of the Exchange Stabilization Fund (ESF) last month to intervene in the yen exchange rate. Bessent said disorderly moves in the yen market could force Japan, a major holder of U.S. Treasuries, to unwind positions, potentially destabilizing global markets and ultimately raising borrowing costs for U.S. households and businesses. He declined to disclose the scale of intervention, confirming only that existing ESF foreign-currency assets were used to buy yen, and had hinted at using euros. Japan spent a record $96.4 billion last month to support the yen. Bessent stressed the actions were legal and compliant, and that the U.S. provided no credit to Japan. In the letter, he repeatedly jabbed at Warren, suggesting she take an "introductory course in international finance." The two have a history of tense exchanges at congressional hearings.
